_readme: English text for animal-details.json, keyed and shaped the same way. Only text fields are here; numbers, links and dates are read from animal-details.json. The detail page uses this file in English and animal-details.json in Chinese, so the two must be kept in step.

traits.length: Head and body: about 150 cm, measured on one captive female (very few specimens)

behavior.food: Herbivore; reported to eat plants such as Schismatoglottis
behavior.breeding: May have a set breeding season (about late August to mid-November); every recorded birth was a single calf, mostly between mid-April and late June

population.scope: Annamite Mountains of Vietnam and Laos (worldwide)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pseudoryx nghetinhensis

traits.length: Body about 2.5 m long, about 1.5 m tall at the shoulder
traits.lifespan: Typically 20–30 years

behavior.food: Herbivore: leaves, buds, grasses, ferns, fruit and fungi
behavior.activity: Mainly active by day, but may also be active for a few hours at night
behavior.social: Largely solitary, coming together only to breed
behavior.breeding: Pregnancy lasts about 440–450 days, usually with a single calf

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Okapia johnstoni

traits.length: Head and body 36–43 cm, tail 56–61 cm

behavior.food: Omnivore: seeds, nuts, fruit, nectar, fungi, wood-boring insect larvae and honey
behavior.activity: Nocturnal and tree-dwelling; the world's largest nocturnal primate
behavior.breeding: Mates at any time of year; females start breeding at about 3–4 years old and have one young every 2–3 years

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Daubentonia madagascariensis

traits.length: Head and body: males 66–76 cm, females 53–62 cm

behavior.food: Mainly fruit and leaves, plus flowers, seeds and a few insects
behavior.social: Usually groups of one adult male with several females and young, as well as all-male groups; one-male groups have 3–19 members, and larger bands reach up to 60

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Nasalis larvatus

traits.length: Head and body 1.2–2 m, 99–125 cm tall at the shoulder
traits.lifespan: No data from the wild; the longest captive record is about 15 years

behavior.food: Mainly grass; may also browse leaves and shoots in the dry season
behavior.social: Females give birth alone, then return to nursery herds of females and young
behavior.breeding: Seasonal breeder; most calves are born in September–November

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Beatragus hunteri

traits.length: Head and body 48–53 cm

behavior.food: Lives in trees and eats leaves
behavior.breeding: No details of mating or breeding have been recorded

population.scope: Only Isla Escudo de Veraguas, Panama
population.trend: A 2012 survey of the coastal mangroves counted only about 79; a 2015 study considered that figure a serious undercount

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Bradypus pygmaeus

traits.length: Head and body 40–65 cm, tail 35–56 cm

behavior.food: Toothless; licks up ants and termites with a long, sticky tongue
behavior.activity: Its eyes are adapted to night vision; mainly active at night
behavior.breeding: 1–2 young a year; mates in autumn and gives birth in a burrow in winter

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Manis javanica

traits.length: Adults 15–45 cm long, most commonly about 23 cm
traits.lifespan: About 10–15 years in the wild

behavior.food: Carnivore: molluscs, worms, aquatic insects, crayfish and small fish, as well as other salamanders

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Ambystoma mexicanum

traits.length: Females 2.6–4.5 m, males 3–6 m

behavior.food: Young gharials eat insects, tadpoles, small fish and frogs
behavior.breeding: Females gather to dig nests in spring and lay 20–95 eggs per clutch

population.trend: The wild population has fallen sharply since the 1930s and now occupies only about 2% of its historical range

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Gavialis gangeticus

traits.lifespan: Lifespan unknown

behavior.breeding: Matures late: a central Pacific study estimated maturity at about 29 years (range 23–36)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Eretmochelys imbricata

traits.length: Up to about 64 cm long
traits.weight: Males about 1.5–3 kg, females about 0.95–1.6 kg
traits.lifespan: Long-lived: average life expectancy about 60 years (±20), with reports of up to 100 years

behavior.food: Entirely herbivorous: fruit, seeds, leaves, stems and rhizomes
behavior.activity: Nocturnal, ground-dwelling and flightless
behavior.breeding: The only parrot that breeds on a lek, with one male mating with several females; males take no part in raising chicks

population.scope: Every known bird is tagged and named; they live on four predator-free islands in New Zealand, plus a 2023 reintroduction to a mainland sanctuary

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Strigops habroptilus

traits.length: Longer overall than any other hornbill (its central tail feathers are especially long)
traits.weight: About 3 kg, of which the casque makes up about 11%

behavior.social: Thought to be territorial and monogamous, but little is known about its social behaviour
behavior.breeding: Breeds once a year, raising one chick each time

threats: According to TRAFFIC, 2,170 casques were seized in just three years in China and Indonesia alone

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Rhinoplax vigil

traits.length: 86–102 cm long
traits.lifespan: Estimated 30–60 years in the wild; the longest captive record is 41 years (Rome Zoo)

behavior.food: An opportunistic top predator that takes whatever local prey is plentiful and easy to catch (not almost exclusively monkeys)
behavior.breeding: Each breeding pair needs a very large home range, which makes the species especially sensitive to deforestation

population.scope: Mindanao only (the island where the species is most numerous)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pithecophaga jefferyi

traits.length: 60–70 cm tall
traits.lifespan: About 10–25 years in the wild; up to about 34 years in captivity

behavior.food: Pursuit diver that mainly eats fish and squid; as sardines declined, its diet shifted partly to anchovies
behavior.social: Colonial, breeding on 27 islands between Namibia and Algoa Bay in South Africa, with two mainland colonies near Cape Town
behavior.breeding: The only penguin that breeds in Africa

population.trend: Estimated at about 1.5 million in 1910; only about 10% remained by the end of the 20th century

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Spheniscus demersus

traits.length: Maximum length: females about 150 cm, males about 140 cm (the smallest living cetacean)
traits.lifespan: Estimated at about 20 years; mature at 3–6 years

behavior.food: Mainly bottom-dwelling fish (such as croakers), plus crustaceans and squid
behavior.social: Usually seen alone or in pairs, often with a calf; small groups of up to 10 have been seen
behavior.breeding: Possibly polygynous, with males competing for females

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Phocoena sinus

behavior.food: Filter feeder: mainly plankton, krill, fish eggs and small schooling fish such as sardines and anchovies
behavior.activity: Highly migratory; gathers seasonally at places such as Ningaloo Reef in Australia, the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, and off Gujarat and Kerala in India
behavior.breeding: Birth has never been observed; mating has been recorded only twice, at Saint Helena

population.trend: The population fell by more than 50% over the past 75 years (the basis of the IUCN assessment)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Rhincodon typus

traits.length: The largest confirmed individual was about 7 m; most today are 2–2.5 m
traits.lifespan: Lifespan unknown; four estimates give 30, 35, 44 and 80 years

behavior.food: Eats fish, molluscs and crustaceans
behavior.activity: Uses its saw to stir up the bottom in search of prey, or slashes through schools of fish
behavior.breeding: Breeds seasonally and gives birth to live young; the timing varies by region

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pristis pristis

traits.length: Disc up to about 7 m across, commonly about 4.5 m

behavior.food: Filters zooplankton such as copepods, mysid shrimp and krill, and occasionally small fish
behavior.activity: An ocean-going species that travels with the currents, alone or in groups of up to 50
behavior.breeding: Males mature at a disc width of about 4 m, females at about 5 m

population.trend: Numbers have dropped sharply over the last 20 years because of overfishing

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Mobula birostris

traits.lifespan: About 15–20 years in the wild; some captive eels have lived more than 80 years

behavior.food: Forages at night by smell: worms, fish, molluscs, crustaceans, and occasionally plankton when it is abundant
behavior.breeding: Spawns in the Sargasso Sea; mating in the wild has never been observed

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Anguilla anguilla

traits.length: Adults about 6 cm long

behavior.food: Tadpoles eat algae and mosquito larvae
behavior.activity: Active by day
behavior.social: Individuals are evenly spaced and do not form large groups

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Phyllobates terribilis

traits.length: 3.1–3.2 m long
traits.weight: The heaviest individuals reach about 2,300 kg
traits.lifespan: About 30–45 years in the wild

behavior.food: Herbivore: shoots, twigs, young leaves and fallen fruit; the most flexible feeder of all rhinos
behavior.social: Largely solitary, apart from mating pairs and mothers with calves

population.scope: Only Ujung Kulon National Park, Indonesia

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Rhinoceros sondaicus

traits.length: Head and body 2.36–3.18 m, 112–145 cm tall at the shoulder
traits.lifespan: Estimated at about 30–45 years in the wild

behavior.social: Largely solitary, together only for courtship and raising young

population.scope: Worldwide; only 5 sizeable wild populations (4 on Sumatra, 1 on Borneo)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Dicerorhinus sumatrensis

traits.length: 1.32–1.8 m tall at the shoulder, 2.8–3.75 m long
traits.lifespan: About 35–50 years without poaching pressure

behavior.food: Plucks leaves and twigs with its pointed, grasping upper lip
behavior.social: Generally considered solitary; the only lasting bond is between mother and calf

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Diceros bicornis

traits.length: Bulls about 2.4–3 m tall at the shoulder, cows about 1.8–2.4 m
traits.weight: Bulls about 4–7 tonnes, cows about 2–4 tonnes (a 2000 study)
traits.lifespan: About 60–70 years

behavior.food: Herbivore; gathers at mineral-rich water holes and salt licks to take in minerals
behavior.social: Matriarchal family groups of up to about 20, made up of adult cows and their offspring
behavior.breeding: Adult bulls join family groups only in the mating season; family members share the care of calves

population.trend: Excessive hunting in the 20th century caused a steep decline

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Loxodonta cyclotis

traits.weight: Bulls average about 4 tonnes, cows about 2.7 tonnes
traits.lifespan: About 60 years in the wild

behavior.food: Herbivore that eats about 150 kg of plants a day, both grazing and browsing
behavior.social: Cows and calves live in herds; bulls live alone or in bachelor groups
behavior.breeding: In the breeding season, bulls temporarily join cow herds to mate

population.trend: Listed as Endangered since 1986; the population has fallen by at least 50% over about 60–75 years (three elephant generations)

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Elephas maximus

traits.weight: Males about 90 kg, females about 45 kg
traits.lifespan: In the wild, females about 44–53 years, males about 47–58 years

behavior.food: Mainly soft fruit; eats more fruit and more insects than the Bornean orangutan
behavior.breeding: Females begin giving birth at about 8 years old

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pongo abelii

traits.weight: Males about 70–90 kg and about 137 cm tall; females about 40–50 kg and about 110 cm tall

behavior.food: An unusual diet that includes caterpillars and conifer cones

population.scope: Worldwide (the species lives only in the Batang Toru area)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pongo tapanuliensis

traits.lifespan: About 35–45 years in the wild; up to about 60 years in captivity

behavior.food: More than 400 kinds of food, including fruit, seeds, flowers, bird eggs, sap and vines
behavior.social: More solitary than the Sumatran orangutan
behavior.breeding: Larger males dominate, but smaller males also breed successfully

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pongo pygmaeus

traits.weight: Males average about 140–200 kg, females about 100 kg

behavior.activity: Lives at 11 sites within an area of about 12,000 km²
behavior.social: Groups usually consist of 1 male, 6–7 females and their young

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Gorilla gorilla diehli

traits.weight: 34–60 kg; males average about 45 kg, females about 33 kg
traits.lifespan: Usually about 40 years in captivity; lifespan in the wild unknown

behavior.food: Mainly fruit
behavior.social: Females usually get first access to food

population.estimate: No exact figure; estimates range from 29,500 to 50,000

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pan paniscus

traits.length: Head and body 51–63.5 cm, tail 28–48.5 cm
traits.weight: About 3.2–15 kg (sources give a wide range)
traits.lifespan: Up to about 14 years in captivity

behavior.food: Mainly bamboo shoots and leaves, plus fruit and flowers
behavior.activity: Solitary and mostly lives in trees; active at night and at dawn and dusk
behavior.breeding: Mates in early spring and gives birth in summer, to up to 4 cubs

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Ailurus fulgens

traits.length: 84–101 cm long, 53–62 cm tall at the shoulder

behavior.food: Highly specialised: mainly hunts rodents of the Afroalpine meadows
behavior.social: Lives in packs; family groups have up to about 20 adults, commonly about 6
behavior.breeding: Apart from the breeding female, reproduction is suppressed in other pack members

population.scope: Only 7 isolated mountain ranges (3,000–4,500 m above sea level), more than half in the Bale Mountains

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Canis simensis

traits.length: Head and body 71–112 cm, 60–75 cm tall at the shoulder
traits.lifespan: About 10–11 years on average in the wild

behavior.food: Specialises in hunting hoofed land mammals, mostly at dawn and dusk, though it is also active by day
behavior.social: Lives in stable packs of 2–27 adults and yearlings
behavior.breeding: Breeding is usually monopolised by the dominant pair

population.scope: Worldwide, spread across 39 subpopulations; the largest may have fewer than 250

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Lycaon pictus

traits.length: Head and body 1.4–2.8 m, tail 0.6–1.1 m, 0.8–1.1 m tall at the shoulder
traits.lifespan: The longest captive record is about 19 years (International Tiger Studbook)

behavior.social: Solitary most of the time; males and females each guard their own home range
behavior.breeding: Tigresses usually have 2–3 cubs, which stay with their mother for about two years

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Panthera tigris

traits.length: Head and body: males about 74.7–82 cm, females about 68.2–77.5 cm
traits.weight: Males about 7–15.9 kg, females about 9.2–10 kg
traits.lifespan: Up to about 13 years in the wild

behavior.food: Mainly European rabbits, supplemented by red-legged partridges and rodents, and occasionally small hoofed animals

population.trend: This was the historic low of 2002, not the current situation; the range has since expanded, with reintroduction projects in several places

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Lynx pardinus

traits.length: Adults average about 2.4 m
traits.weight: 240–400 kg (males average about 320 kg, females about 300 kg)
traits.lifespan: Up to about 45 years, averaging about 20–25 years

behavior.food: Forages by day for fish, crustaceans and molluscs (mainly octopus, squid, lobster, mullet, flatfish, tuna, sardines and eels), eating up to about 3 kg a day
behavior.breeding: No fixed breeding season: pups are born all year round, most in September–November; mature at about 4 years old

population.scope: Scattered across the Aegean Sea, the Madeira Islands and Cap Blanc between Mauritania and Western Sahara

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Monachus monachus

traits.length: Males about 2.1 m long, females about 2.4 m
traits.weight: Males about 140–180 kg, females about 180–270 kg
traits.lifespan: Up to about 25–30 years

behavior.food: Mainly bony reef fish, plus cephalopods and crustaceans

population.trend: A 2010 estimate put the population at only about 1,100

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Neomonachus schauinslandi

traits.length: Adults average 13–18 m
traits.lifespan: Estimated at 70 years or more; but a 2024 study found an average lifespan of only about 22 years, possibly linked to losses caused by whaling

behavior.activity: Migrates between feeding grounds in the Labrador Sea and winter calving grounds off Georgia and Florida

population.estimate: About 380, of which about 70 are breeding females

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Eubalaena glacialis

traits.length: The largest confirmed length is about 30 m
traits.lifespan: At least 40–45 years (long-term photo-identification studies in the northeast Pacific)

behavior.food: Filter feeder whose diet is almost entirely krill
behavior.activity: Generally migrates seasonally, feeding near the poles in summer and moving to breeding grounds near the tropics in winter
behavior.social: Usually alone or in small groups, with no clear social structure beyond mother and calf

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Balaenoptera musculus

traits.length: For the blue whale species as a whole, the largest confirmed length is about 30 m
traits.weight: For the blue whale species as a whole, up to about 190–200 tonnes
traits.lifespan: For the blue whale species as a whole, at least 40–45 years

behavior.food: For the blue whale species as a whole, the diet is almost entirely krill

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Balaenoptera musculus intermedia

traits.lifespan: More than 70 years

behavior.food: Herbivore that grazes seagrass from the seabed with its downturned snout
behavior.breeding: Breeds very slowly

population.scope: Only the Gulf of Carpentaria in Australia's Northern Territory (a regional figure, not worldwide)
population.trend: The worldwide population is generally thought to have fallen by about 20% over the last 90 years, but the total is uncertain

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Dugong dugon

traits.length: Males up to about 2.5 m long
traits.weight: Males up to about 185 kg (males are about 16% longer and 55% heavier than females)
traits.lifespan: Lifespan in the wild unknown; healthy captive animals have lived 10–30 years

behavior.food: A very broad diet of up to 53 fish species, such as croakers, catfish, characins and piranhas
behavior.social: Usually seen alone or in pairs; groups rarely exceed 8
behavior.activity: In the rainy season the sexes separate: males mostly stay in river channels, while females with calves use flooded areas

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Inia geoffrensis

traits.lifespan: The oldest recorded individual was a 28-year-old male, 199 cm long

population.scope: Indus River, Pakistan (survey by the Sindh Wildlife Department)
population.trend: Estimated at about 1,800 in 2017 (about 1,200 in 2001)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Platanista minor

traits.length: Males about 200–250 cm long
traits.lifespan: Up to about 30 years

behavior.food: Mostly carnivorous, specialising in hunting seals, especially ringed seals
behavior.social: Usually solitary, though bears may gather on land
behavior.breeding: In the breeding season, males guard females and keep rivals away

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Ursus maritimus

traits.length: 1.2–1.9 m long

behavior.food: Feeds almost entirely on bamboo.
behavior.social: Solitary, coming together only in the mating season
behavior.breeding: Females raise their cubs for 18–24 months on average

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

Giant panda.habitat: Mountain bamboo forests of central and western China, in parts of the mountain ranges of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu.

population.estimate: About 1,864 (adults and subadults, not including cubs)
population.scope: Wild population in China (Fourth National Giant Panda Survey)
population.trend: The 2016 IUCN assessment marked the population trend as "increasing"; this reflects the wild population only, not captive animals.

threats: Roads, development and farming divide its habitat, cutting the population into small, isolated patches.
Climate change may affect where bamboo grows and how well it grows.
Giant panda.ecology: The giant panda is often treated as an "umbrella species": protecting the bamboo and mountain forests it depends on also protects many other plants and animals that live alongside it.
conservation: Since 2021, China has been building Giant Panda National Park, joining previously separate reserves into a larger whole.
In 2016 the IUCN moved it from "Endangered" to "Vulnerable", a sign that conservation work is paying off, though its habitat still needs continued protection.

didYouKnow.text: The giant panda's "sixth finger" is really a specialised wrist bone (the radial sesamoid). Working with the first digit, it lets the panda grip bamboo nimbly.
didYouKnow.source: Widely reported in reputable popular-science sources; see the sources below.

traits.length: About 60–85 cm long
traits.lifespan: About 13–18 years in the wild (males face greater risks and may live shorter lives)

behavior.food: Mainly eats eucalyptus leaves, and usually lives in open eucalypt woodland
behavior.social: Not social; the only bond is between a mother and her dependent young
behavior.breeding: After birth, the young spends its first 6–7 months in the pouch

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Phascolarctos cinereus

traits.lifespan: Few live longer than 5 years in the wild

behavior.food: Carnivore; the largest living carnivorous marsupial
behavior.social: Usually solitary, but sometimes several feed together in one place
behavior.breeding: Pregnancy lasts about three weeks and produces 20–30 young; the young leave the pouch after about 100 days

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Sarcophilus harrisii

traits.length: About 35 cm tall and up to about 1 m long

behavior.food: Eats native grasses and various roots; spends little time feeding each day (about 6 hours in winter, about 2 hours in summer)
behavior.activity: Nocturnal, living in networks of underground burrows
behavior.breeding: Females are slightly larger than males

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Lasiorhinus krefftii

traits.length: Head and body 39–46 cm, tail 56–63 cm
traits.lifespan: The longest record in the wild is a female that lived 20 years; females rarely live beyond 16

behavior.food: Omnivore; the most ground-adapted of all living lemurs
behavior.social: Lives in groups ("troops") of up to about 30

population.scope: Wild population in Madagascar (possibly as low as this figure)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Lemur catta

traits.length: Head and body 40–42 cm, tail 45–48 cm
traits.weight: Males average about 2.75 kg, females about 2.61 kg

behavior.food: A bamboo specialist: woody bamboo makes up as much as 95% of its diet, plus fruit, flowers and other grasses; its food contains high levels of cyanide
behavior.social: Lives in groups of up to about 28; the only lemur in which males are dominant
behavior.breeding: Females first give birth at 2–3 years old; mothers forage carrying their young on their backs or in their mouths

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Prolemur simus

traits.length: Wingspan about 3.0 m, the widest of any North American bird
traits.lifespan: Can live up to about 60 years, one of the longest-lived birds in the world

behavior.food: Scavenger that eats large amounts of carrion
behavior.social: Large groups have a developed social hierarchy, with pecking order settled through body language, competitive play, hisses and grunts

population.trend: In 1987 all 27 remaining wild birds were taken into captivity; captive breeding then increased their numbers, and releases to the wild began in 1991

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Gymnogyps californianus

traits.length: Wingspan about 2–2.3 m; the tallest bird in North America
traits.lifespan: Estimated at 22–30 years or more in the wild

population.scope: Wild migratory population (between coastal Texas and Canada's Northwest Territories, known as the Aransas–Wood Buffalo population)
population.trend: About 140 more live in two reintroduced wild populations in Wisconsin and Louisiana; all populations together (including captive birds) total just over 830

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Grus americana

traits.length: About 33 cm long, wingspan 46–52 cm
traits.lifespan: Up to 40–60 years in captivity; about 23 years on average in the wild

behavior.food: Mainly fruit, plus nuts and seeds (including oil-palm fruit); sometimes feeds on the ground

population.estimate: Estimated at between 630,000 and 13 million, very uncertain
population.trend: A 2015 study found the Ghana population almost "wiped out", down 90–99% since 1992

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Psittacus erithacus

traits.length: 100–140 cm long, wingspan 230–260 cm

behavior.food: Mainly fish, but also hunts many other wetland vertebrates
behavior.social: Solitary, a habit that extends to its breeding behaviour
behavior.breeding: Both parents incubate the eggs, shade, guard and feed the chicks

population.scope: Most live in the swamps of South Sudan, Uganda, the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Balaeniceps rex

traits.length: 1.1–1.5 m long, wingspan 1.9–2.1 m
traits.lifespan: About 10–15 years in the wild; up to about 19 years in captivity

behavior.food: Hunts on the ground, often stamping prey to death; eats insects and small vertebrates
behavior.social: Up to 50 may gather at water holes in dry areas, or where rodents or locusts are swarming
behavior.breeding: May breed at any time of year, mostly late in the dry season; nests on top of thorny trees, with 1–3 eggs per clutch

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Sagittarius serpentarius

traits.length: 78–98 cm long, wingspan 1.96–2.25 m

behavior.food: Its bill cannot tear tough hide, so it eats only soft tissue such as internal organs
behavior.social: A social vulture that relies on others of its kind for information about food and carcasses

population.trend: The most widespread and common vulture in Africa, but declining fast; in one survey area, breeding pairs fell from 73 in 2007 to 22 in 2017

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Gyps africanus

traits.length: 62–72 cm long, wingspan 155–180 cm

behavior.food: Scavenger of carcasses and refuse; circles over savanna and settlements looking for rubbish dumps and slaughterhouses
behavior.social: Can form loose colonies; in West Africa 50–250 often feed together, while in southern Africa it is solitary and secretive
behavior.breeding: Builds a stick nest in a tree (often a palm) and lays 1 egg at a time

population.trend: Populations in areas such as Dakar, Senegal, have lost more than 85% over the past 50 years

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Necrosyrtes monachus

traits.lifespan: Up to about 51 years in captivity; at least 21 years in the wild

behavior.food: Mainly a scavenger, but also opportunistically hunts small mammals, birds and reptiles; eats other birds' eggs, throwing stones to crack large ones
behavior.activity: Populations that breed in temperate regions migrate south in winter; tropical populations are relatively sedentary
behavior.breeding: In the Spanish population, young birds fledge after 90–110 days

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Neophron percnopterus

behavior.food: Omnivore; eats crops such as peanuts, millet and bean pods in farmland
behavior.social: Solitary in the breeding season; forms small flocks in winter

population.trend: About 250 in 2011; it has disappeared from about 90% of its former range

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Ardeotis nigriceps

traits.length: 66–68 cm long, about 55 cm tall
traits.weight: Females about 1.7–1.9 kg, males about 1.2–1.5 kg

behavior.activity: Moves only short distances, perhaps a few tens of kilometres, and spends most of its time on its breeding grounds; easiest to see in the March–August breeding season, most often early in the morning and in the evening

population.scope: Worldwide; the South Asian population has fewer than 350 adults, about 85% of them in India

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Houbaropsis bengalensis

traits.length: 14–16 cm long

behavior.food: Sweeps its bill from side to side as it feeds; on the breeding grounds it eats small animals such as mosquitoes, flies, beetles and spiders

population.trend: The breeding population has fallen markedly since the 1970s

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Calidris pygmaea

behavior.food: Mainly seeds, buds, fruit, nuts and herbaceous plants
behavior.breeding: Eggs are white, usually 2 per clutch, and both parents incubate them

population.trend: And thought to be still declining

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Cacatua sulphurea

traits.length: Up to about 25 cm long

behavior.food: Eats fruit, seeds, worms and insects
behavior.social: Young birds often move in flocks, which helps them find food and watch for predators
behavior.breeding: Breeds in Bali's rainy season: males call loudly and bob their heads to attract females; nests in tree holes, where the female lays and incubates 2–3 eggs

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Leucopsar rothschildi

traits.length: About 20 cm long

behavior.food: Eats the seeds and berries of small coastal grasses and shrubs
behavior.activity: One of only three migratory parrots; breeds only in south-west Tasmania and winters on the southern coast of mainland Australia

population.trend: Only 14 remained in the wild in February 2017; several organisations run captive-breeding programmes

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Neophema chrysogaster

behavior.food: Mainly nectar from eucalypts and mistletoe, plus insects, honeydew and fruit
behavior.breeding: Breeds mainly from August to January, matching the flowering of key eucalypts and mistletoe

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Anthochaera phrygia

traits.length: 62–79 cm tall

behavior.food: Mainly fish
behavior.social: Usually nests in separate pairs or loose small groups, not in large colonies like other penguins
behavior.breeding: For the first six weeks after hatching, one parent guards the chicks by day while the other forages at sea

population.trend: Numbers on the Otago Peninsula have fallen by 75% since the mid-1990s; the trend suggests it could disappear locally from the peninsula within the next 20–40 years

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Megadyptes antipodes

traits.length: 48–50 cm tall
traits.lifespan: 15–20 years, possibly shorter in the wild because of predators and other factors

behavior.food: Eats fish and crustaceans in the waters fed by the Cromwell Current
behavior.breeding: Monogamous and can breed at any time of year; parents take turns guarding the nest and foraging at sea

population.year: Average population of about 1,500 birds in 1993–2003

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Spheniscus mendiculus

traits.length: About 85 cm long (including tail feathers), wingspan about 90 cm
traits.lifespan: Can live more than 50 years in captivity

behavior.social: Mostly in monogamous pairs, also in small flocks of 7–9; one large roost of 70 birds is known
behavior.breeding: Usually breeds once a year; if eggs or chicks are lost, it may lay again in the same season

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Ara glaucogularis

traits.length: 70–75 cm long
traits.lifespan: The highest captive record is 38.3 years

behavior.food: Mainly the nuts of the licuri palm (Syagrus coronata), eating up to 350 a day, plus other seeds and agave flowers; also takes farmers' maize
behavior.social: Often forages in flocks
behavior.breeding: The breeding season begins with the summer rains early in the year, and the young leave the nest in May

population.trend: Under stronger protection, the worldwide population grew about thirtyfold in the first two decades of the 21st century

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Anodorhynchus leari

behavior.food: Mainly hunts tree-dwelling mammals, above all sloths; females can snatch howler monkeys, spider monkeys or adult sloths of 6–9 kg in flight
behavior.breeding: Nests and hunts in the upper canopy (the emergent layer) of tropical lowland rainforest

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Harpia harpyja

traits.length: Wingspan up to about 3.3 m
traits.weight: Up to about 15 kg, averaging about 11.3 kg (males about 12.5, females about 10.1)
traits.lifespan: Some individuals live more than 70 years

behavior.food: Mainly a scavenger
behavior.social: Large groups have a developed social hierarchy, with pecking order settled through body language, competitive play and calls
behavior.breeding: Usually lays 1–2 eggs per clutch

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Vultur gryphus

traits.length: About 1 m tall, wingspan about 2 m

behavior.food: Omnivore: plants, seeds, grain, insects, frogs, worms, snakes, small fish and the eggs of aquatic animals
behavior.activity: Has no fixed migration route; birds nearer the tropics are mostly resident

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Balearica regulorum

traits.length: 70–80 cm long, wingspan 125–135 cm
traits.lifespan: 20–25 years on average in captivity (the oldest male lived 37 years, the oldest female 30)

behavior.food: Forages in semi-arid steppe and fallow fields, eating small animals such as lizards and insects
behavior.social: Breeds in colonies on sea or mountain cliffs
behavior.breeding: Builds stick nests, usually with 2–3 eggs per clutch

population.trend: The Birecik colony in Turkey had about 500 breeding pairs in the first half of the 20th century, and about 3,000 birds around 1930; numbers crashed in the 1970s. Recent reintroductions brought Turkey's semi-wild colony close to 250 birds in 2018

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Geronticus eremita

behavior.food: Zooplankton, small fish and crabs, caught by diving and swimming with its wings
behavior.social: Breeds in clifftop colonies
behavior.breeding: Digs a burrow to nest in and lays a single white egg

population.scope: More than 90% of the worldwide population is in Europe; Iceland's colonies hold about 60% of the world total

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Fratercula arctica

traits.length: Adults average about 70 cm
traits.weight: About 5.5 kg on average (varying greatly with season and sex)

behavior.food: Eats krill and other crustaceans, plus small fish and cephalopods; consumes more marine life each year than any other seabird
behavior.social: Breeding colonies reach up to about 100,000 birds, among the densest of any penguin

population.year: An older estimate; later assessments show numbers have declined

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Eudyptes chrysolophus

traits.length: Adults 1.5–2.1 m long
traits.lifespan: Can exceed 50 years; up to about 70 years in captivity

behavior.food: Opportunistic feeder, mainly eating fish and invertebrates
behavior.activity: Nocturnal in summer; spends the winter dormant in burrows
behavior.breeding: Mates in early summer; females usually lay 20–30 eggs, the smallest eggs of any crocodilian

population.trend: About 1,000 in the wild in the 1970s, falling to fewer than 130 in 2001, with a recovery after 2003

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Alligator sinensis

traits.length: Young 1.2–1.5 m, adults 2.1–3 m

behavior.food: Adults mainly eat fish and snakes, plus amphibians and small mammals
behavior.breeding: In captive observations it breeds in the rainy season (April–May), laying 15–50 eggs and guarding them until they hatch; the female helps the young out of their shells and carries them to the water in her mouth

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Crocodylus siamensis

traits.length: Adults rarely exceed 2.7 m, with a maximum record of about 3.5 m; can breed at about 1.5 m
traits.weight: Adults rarely exceed 90 kg; can breed at about 15 kg

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Crocodylus mindorensis

traits.length: Males of up to 6.8 m were once reported; the more widely accepted maximum is about 5.2 m, and large males today are about 4.2 m
traits.weight: Large males up to about 450 kg, females up to about 225 kg
traits.lifespan: Possibly 70–80 years without persecution

behavior.food: A top predator that favours fish but has a flexible diet, taking birds, mammals and reptiles, occasionally including caimans
behavior.social: Females guard their group of young, usually for about a year and sometimes for more than three
behavior.breeding: Digs holes in sand to lay its eggs

population.trend: Thousands were killed in the Orinoco River and the Llanos wetlands from the 1940s to the 1960s, bringing it close to extinction

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Crocodylus intermedius

traits.length: Shell 26–38 cm long
traits.lifespan: The longest record is 188 years (an estimated age, for a tortoise named Tu'i Malila)

behavior.food: Herbivore; grass makes up 80–90% of its diet, along with fruit and succulents
behavior.breeding: Females lay 3–12 eggs at a time, bury them in a hole about 15–20 cm deep and then leave

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Astrochelys radiata

traits.length: Males have a shell up to about 43 cm long

behavior.food: Grazes on open rocky ground among bamboo thickets, and has been seen eating the dried dung of animals such as bushpigs

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Astrochelys yniphora

traits.length: Adults more than 100 cm long and more than 70 cm wide

behavior.food: Eats fish, crabs, snails and frogs, as well as aquatic plants such as water hyacinth
behavior.breeding: Usually lays 20–80 eggs per clutch, mostly at night or early in the morning

population.trend: In the six breeding seasons before 2013, 80 eggs were laid and none hatched; in 2008 a fertile female was moved to Suzhou Zoo to pair with the only known captive male (about 100 years old)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Rafetus swinhoei

traits.length: Up to about 2.7 m long
traits.lifespan: Little is known about its lifespan

behavior.food: Mainly eats jellyfish, feeding in cooler waters
behavior.activity: Pacific leatherbacks migrate about 9,700 km from nesting beaches in Indonesia to feed on jellyfish off California; the deepest recorded dive is about 1,280 m

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Dermochelys coriacea

traits.length: Shell 58–70 cm long

behavior.food: Eats molluscs, crustaceans (floating crabs and shrimp), jellyfish, fish, algae and sea urchins; young turtles feed mainly at the surface, while adults forage opportunistically on the seabed, mainly for crabs
behavior.breeding: Most females return each year to the same beach, Rancho Nuevo in Tamaulipas, Mexico, to nest

population.trend: Nesting females are estimated to have fallen from about 89,000 in 1947 to about 7,702 in 1985

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Lepidochelys kempii

traits.length: Adult shells average about 90 cm
traits.weight: Adults average about 135 kg, up to about 200 kg
traits.lifespan: Takes 17–33 years to mature; estimated maximum lifespan in the wild 47–67 years

behavior.food: Omnivore, mainly eating invertebrates on the seabed
behavior.breeding: Low reproductive rate: after laying about 4 clutches on average, a female rests for 2–3 years before nesting again

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Caretta caretta

traits.length: Males up to about 3 m long
traits.weight: Males up to about 150 kg; wild adults usually about 70 kg
traits.lifespan: Matures at 8–11 years and is estimated to live about 30 years (some estimates reach 62)

behavior.food: Adults mainly eat Javan deer and wild boar, along with a great deal of carrion
behavior.activity: Cold-blooded; most active by day, with some activity at night
behavior.social: Solitary, coming together only to breed and feed
behavior.breeding: Mates in May–August and lays eggs in September, up to about 20 at a time, in abandoned megapode nests or in holes it digs itself; incubation takes about 7–8 months, and the young hatch the following April

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Varanus komodoensis

traits.length: Males are clearly longer
traits.weight: The maximum weight of adult males varies by island, from 12 kg on southern Isabela to 1 kg on Genovesa
traits.lifespan: Up to 60 years, but the average lifespan is 12 years or less

behavior.food: Eats almost nothing but algae; large males dive to feed, while females and smaller males feed in the intertidal zone at low tide
behavior.social: Lives in colonies on rocky shores, usually of 20–500 and sometimes more than 1,000
behavior.breeding: Large males hold territories for short periods, while smaller males use other breeding strategies; females dig holes in the soil to lay eggs, which hatch on their own months later

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Amblyrhynchus cristatus

traits.length: Females 45–63 mm, males 35–48 mm
traits.lifespan: About 12 years

behavior.food: Tadpoles eat algae and take about 6–7 months to develop
behavior.social: Males are fairly solitary and aggressive; they communicate with other amphibians using throat calls and "waving"

population.captive: Captive-breeding programmes run at more than 50 institutions in North America and Panama
population.trend: The El Copé population collapsed rapidly in 2004 because of chytrid fungus disease

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Atelopus zeteki

traits.length: Snout–vent length up to about 22 cm; typical adults 17–18 cm
traits.lifespan: About 12 years; mature at about 3 years

behavior.food: Strictly carnivorous: mainly insects such as crickets, plus millipedes, crustaceans, spiders, and even small vertebrates such as frogs, snakes and bats
behavior.activity: Ground-dwelling and nocturnal
behavior.breeding: After the tadpoles hatch, the mother lays up to about 25,000 unfertilised "food eggs" for them to eat

population.trend: The population fell by at least 80% in 1995–2004; almost none remain in the wild on Montserrat, and the species depends on captive-breeding programmes at several zoos

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Leptodactylus fallax

traits.length: Adults average about 1.3 m, up to about 1.8 m
traits.weight: Adults average about 25–30 kg, up to about 50 kg

behavior.food: Eats insects, millipedes, amphibians, freshwater crabs, shrimp, fish and water shrews
behavior.activity: Most individuals stop feeding when the water is warmer than 20°C, and almost none feed at 28°C

population.trend: The wild population is estimated to have fallen by more than 80% since the 1950s

china.note: Under China's List of Wild Animals under State Key Protection.

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Andrias davidianus

traits.length: Up to about 6 m long, commonly about 1.25 m

behavior.activity: Spends most of its life at sea and migrates up rivers to spawn

population.estimate: Fewer than 800 mature individuals (no specific population estimate)
population.year: At the time of assessment (2020) estimated at 20–750 mature individuals

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Acipenser sturio

traits.length: Up to about 3 m long
traits.weight: Grows extremely fast, reaching 150–200 kg in about 6 years

behavior.food: Young fish eat zooplankton (including each other); after about a year they become herbivores, eating filamentous algae
behavior.activity: Gathers and swims upriver to spawn at the start of the rainy season (its migration is not yet fully understood)

population.trend: Catch data show the population fell by about 80% over 14 years (older data)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Pangasianodon gigas

traits.length: Typical individuals are at least about 3.5 m long, up to about 4.6 m
traits.weight: Typical individuals weigh more than 230 kg; the heaviest record is about 449.5 kg
traits.lifespan: Typically 20–30 years; one recorded female was estimated at 40–50 years old

behavior.food: A powerful, solitary top predator that eats crustaceans, cephalopods, bony fish and smaller sharks
behavior.activity: Migratory; populations off Florida and in the South China Sea move towards the poles in summer
behavior.social: Solitary
behavior.breeding: Gives birth to live young every two years, 2–49 pups per litter

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Sphyrna mokarran

traits.length: The largest individuals exceed 4 m, but most reach about 3 m at most
traits.lifespan: The longest captive record is just over 3 years (a female at Monterey Bay Aquarium)

behavior.food: Mainly ocean-going cephalopods such as squid, and bony fish such as lancetfish, jacks, dolphinfish, marlin, tuna and mackerel
behavior.activity: Spends most of its time within the top 150 m of the ocean, preferring deep offshore waters
behavior.social: Usually solitary, but large numbers gather where food is concentrated
behavior.breeding: Gives birth to live young; in the northwest Atlantic and southwest Indian Ocean it mostly mates and gives birth in early summer, while in the Pacific pregnant females are found all year round

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Carcharhinus longimanus

traits.length: Up to about 2.5 m long
traits.lifespan: Reaches maturity at about 9–12 years

behavior.food: An opportunistic predator of many kinds of fish, crustaceans, cephalopods and salps
behavior.activity: Feeds in temperate southern waters around Australia in winter, and from spring to autumn migrates to tropical waters in the north-west Indian Ocean to spawn

population.trend: Australian catches peaked in 1982 (about 21,500 tonnes); since then the total population is estimated to have fallen by about 92% (an older estimate)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Thunnus maccoyii

behavior.food: Can also feed by filtering food from the water (especially when bleached or when the water stays murky for long periods)
behavior.breeding: Releases eggs and sperm into the water on only a few nights through "broadcast spawning"; after fertilisation the larvae settle on hard surfaces and grow into new colonies

population.trend: The population fell by about 97% between 1980 and 2006 (the estimate when it was listed under the US Endangered Species Act)

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Acropora palmata

traits.length: Healthy mature colonies can grow more than 2 m tall and wide

behavior.food: Catches zooplankton at night with long tentacles, while also getting energy from the symbiotic zooxanthellae living in its tissue
behavior.breeding: Eggs and sperm are released together in one synchronised event

population.trend: White band disease (first found in 1979) is thought to be the main cause of the decline of shallow reef-building corals such as staghorn and elkhorn coral over the past 30 years, a decline of up to about 95%

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Acropora cervicornis

traits.lifespan: A colony lasts about 4–5 months; queens live about 77 days on average

behavior.food: The queen first gathers nectar and pollen to feed the first batch of larvae
behavior.social: Colonies usually have 50–400 bees; captive colonies can be larger
behavior.breeding: The queen fertilises her eggs with sperm stored from mating the previous autumn; eggs hatch in about 4 days and become adults within 5 weeks at most

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Bombus affinis

traits.length: Wingspan 8.9–10.2 cm
traits.lifespan: Adults usually live 2–5 weeks during the breeding season

behavior.food: Caterpillars feed on milkweed
behavior.activity: Each late summer and autumn, the eastern North American population migrates thousands of kilometres from the northern and central United States and southern Canada to Florida and Mexico; later generations return in spring
behavior.breeding: Complete metamorphosis in four stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and adult; from egg to adult takes as little as about 25 days in warm summers and up to 7 weeks in cool springs

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Danaus plexippus

traits.length: Shell up to about 20 cm long, typically 10–14 cm
traits.lifespan: Estimated to live 25–75 years; starts breeding at 3–7 years old

behavior.food: A herbivorous sea snail that mainly eats drifting algae and kelp
behavior.activity: A broadcast spawner: successful breeding needs individuals to live close to one another
behavior.breeding: Spawns in spring and early summer, occasionally again in autumn

population.trend: At many sites more than 90% have disappeared, and at some the population has vanished entirely

sources.label: IUCN Red List (search by scientific name): Haliotis cracherodii
